paper.title: Bounded (O(1)) Regret Recommendation Learning via Synthetic Controls Oracle

settings.name_in_paper: Recommender system with repeatedly arriving users, linear factor reward model and Synthetic Control Oracle
unmapped: Finite set of users A with fixed contexts who arrive repeatedly according to general (renewal-type) arrival processes, not necessarily i.i.d. sampling
Disjoint linear factor reward model mu_{j,m} = phi_m(x_j)'beta_m + psi_m(y_j)'lambda_m with unobservable covariates y_j; the representation phi is unknown
Learner has access to a Synthetic Control Oracle returning coefficients a_ji with mu_jm = sum_i a_ji mu_im (Assumption 1)
Some users opt out of data tracking; only opted-in users' data are shared
Regret is per user, against that user's optimal arm
settings.definition_quote: Let $Y_{j,m}(k)$ denote the reward obtained from user $j$'s $k$th pull of arm $m$. We first consider the reward model $Y_{j,m}(k)=\phi_m(\mathbf{x}_j)'\beta_m+\psi_m(\mathbf{y}_j)'\lambda_m+\epsilon(k)=\mu_{j,m}+\epsilon(k)$ ... the finite time pseudo-regret of user $j$ until time $T$ is $Regret_{j}(T):=\sum_{n=1}^{N_j(T)} \Delta_{j, m_j(n)}$

symbols.k_c: constant k appearing in the bound (from the 1/n^2 arrival condition of Assumption 3, per the proof)
symbols.Delta_i: gap Delta_{j,m} of arm m for the fixed user j

conditions: Assumption 3: |E_{j,m} ∩ A_+ ∩ A_m| >= d for all opted-in j and all m (enough opted-in users with comparable arrival rates)
user j is opted in (j in A_+)
tuning: self-experience width sqrt(ln N_j(t)/N_{j,m}(t)); counterfactual width sqrt((2 ln d + 4 ln N_j(t)) c_{m,t}^2 / N^min_{j,m}(t))

source.label: prop:BoundedRegret
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{assumption: SCO} and \ref{ass: Arrivalcondition}, $E[Regret_{j}(T)]\le \sum_{m\in M} \Delta_{j,m} \left(\frac{\pi^2|A||M|}{6}+ \frac{k\pi^2|A|}{6}\right)$ for $j\in A_+$. Since this bound does not increase with $T$, the system expected regret $\sum_{j\in A}E[Regret_{j}(T)]$ is bounded.

results.notes: Per-user bounded regret. Regret is defined through gaps, so pseudo-regret. The meaning of k is ambiguous: the paper uses k for the number of covariates, but in the proof it appears as the constant from the limsup in Assumption 3. The sum is effectively over suboptimal arms, since the optimal arm has zero gap. Corollary 1 restates this result qualitatively.
